content_units: Best Fit for a CS Student

For your priorities—  battery life, portability, and enough power for coding + light Docker + occasional photo editing  —the best overall pick is the   ASUS Zenbook 14 OLED  . It balances the strongest battery setup, very good portability, and the most modern all-around platform under your   $1000 cap  .
Ranked Laptop Comparison
Rank   Laptop   Price   Weight   Battery   Why it ranks here
1   ASUS Zenbook 14 OLED   $999   1.28 kg   75Wh   Best balance of battery, portability, and performance; strongest fit for student use
2   HP Pavilion Aero 13   $920   0.99 kg   43Wh   Best for ultra-light carry; strong CPU, but smaller battery hurts endurance
3   Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5   $780   1.46 kg   57Wh   Best value pick; solid battery and performance, but less premium and less portable than top two
4   Acer Aspire 5   $729   1.8 kg   50Wh   Good storage and decent power, but heavier and less portable for daily campus use
Why the Ranking Comes Out This Way
1) ASUS Zenbook 14 OLED — Best overall
Why it wins
-   75Wh battery   is the biggest here, which matters a lot for classes, coding sessions, and library use.
-   1.28 kg   is very portable for a 14-inch laptop.
-   Core Ultra 5 125H   is a modern chip with good efficiency and enough performance for IDEs, browser tabs, programming tools, light containers, and photo editing.
- 14-inch size is a sweet spot: more comfortable than 13.3-inch for coding, but still easy to carry.
Tradeoffs
- It is the   most expensive   option and sits right at your budget cap.
- OLED is great visually, but depending on brightness/use, real-world battery can vary more than with a standard IPS panel.
Best for
- Students who want the most complete “carry all day, code all day” option.
2) HP Pavilion Aero 13 — Best if portability is your top priority
Why it’s excellent
-   0.99 kg   is dramatically lighter than the others; you will feel this difference every day.
-   Ryzen 7 8840U   is a very capable efficient chip for coding, multitasking, light Docker, and moderate creative work.
- Compact 13.3-inch design is great for commuting and tight lecture hall desks.
Tradeoffs
-   43Wh battery   is the smallest battery here, so despite an efficient processor, endurance is less reassuring than the Zenbook.
- 13.3-inch is portable, but some students find it a bit cramped for long coding sessions unless using an external monitor.
Best for
- Students who walk a lot, commute often, and care most about low bag weight.
3) Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5 — Best value
Why it’s a smart buy
- At   $780  , it gives you   Ryzen 7, 16GB RAM, and 512GB SSD   for much less than the Zenbook.
-   57Wh battery   is respectable.
- 14-inch and   1.46 kg   still make it portable enough for student use.
Tradeoffs
- The   Ryzen 7 7730U   is competent, but less modern than the Ryzen 8840U and Core Ultra 5 125H.
- It is a bit heavier than the Zenbook and clearly less premium overall.
- For photo editing and Docker, it is fine—but it has less headroom than the top two.
Best for
- Students who want the best   price-to-performance   choice and would rather save  $200.
4) Acer Aspire 5 — Good budget power, weakest fit for your priorities
What it does well
-   1TB SSD   is the most storage here, which is useful for projects, datasets, Docker images, and photos.
- The   i5-13420H   should feel reasonably snappy for coding.
Tradeoffs
-   1.8 kg   is the heaviest by a clear margin.
-   15.6-inch   size is less convenient for carrying around campus.
-   50Wh battery   is not especially strong for a larger laptop.
- This laptop makes more sense for desk use than all-day portability.
Best for
- Someone who wants a cheaper, larger machine with more storage and doesn’t mind carrying extra weight.
Final Recommendation by Priority
If I optimize strictly for your stated order:
1.   Battery life
2.   Portability
3.   Enough power for coding, light Docker, and occasional photo editing
Then the ranking stays:
1.   ASUS Zenbook 14 OLED
2.   HP Pavilion Aero 13
3.   Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5
4.   Acer Aspire 5
Best overall choice
ASUS Zenbook 14 OLED
- Best battery setup
- Still very light
- Strong modern performance
- Best all-around student machine under $1000
Best alternative if you want to spend less
Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5
- Best value
- Gives up some battery/portability polish, but still very capable
Best alternative if you care most about carrying comfort
HP Pavilion Aero 13
- Lightest by far
- Excellent for travel and daily commuting
- Just be aware of the smaller battery
